citation.authors: Gu Y, McNamara JA Jr, Sigler LM, Baccetti T
citation.title: Comparison of craniofacial characteristics of typical Chinese and Caucasian young adults

population.label: Caucasian (European background; used for Australian patients of European background)

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 6 differences, all definitionMatch; every mean, SD and n agreed). All 38 values re-read from the page image of Table 2 (p. 207, PDF p. 3): agree. Decisions as gu2011 (merge notes): #31 close and + 90; #23 close; #57 close; Wits close with 'occlusal plane not stated in the paper' (owner 7 Oct). Selection class-I-balanced (a 'ideal-aesthetic'). Scale enlarged 8%, p. 206. Men's maxillomandibular difference 37.2 (Table 2) kept, Table 4's 37.3 in the note (merge notes). No age band at first; a's computed ageMean (23.3) dropped. Fix round 1 (2026-10-08, owner AGE-1 / MAL-1, rulings P42, P45, P47, review): ageBand [18, 40] on every row (owner AGE-1). Wording (Task 9b-1, re-review minors): the age caveat says the ruling once.

caveats: The Michigan Caucasian comparison group of Gu 2011 (owner 7 Oct: the Caucasian Wits norm): untreated adults of North European ancestry from McNamara & Ellis 1988 and McNamara et al. 1993, inclusion criteria 'virtually identical' to the Chinese sample (p. 206). Men 24.1 ± 5.7 y (n 30), women 22.9 ± 5.2 y (n 60).

8% film enlargement: p. 206 says every cephalogram was standardised to 8 per cent magnification. Read as the mm values including an 8% enlargement (as McNamara 1984's 'enlargement factor included', whose samples and software the paper shares); stored as printed and converted to true size by the resolver (owner M-1, ruling P27).

No age range is printed (only mean ± SD by sex). Age band 18–40 on every row by owner ruling 8 Oct (AGE-1, age first): the paper gives mean ages 24.1 ± 5.7 (M) / 22.9 ± 5.2 (F), adults, no range printed; band 18–40 (P18: upper bound not stated; 40 by convention).

The paper does not define its mandibular plane ('MP', IMPA), occlusal plane (Wits), facial-axis points or incisor points; it cites Ricketts 1968 and McNamara 1984 and used Dentofacial Planner (p. 206). Those rows are close.
Head position during filming not stated. Lateral headfilms hand traced, landmarks verified by a second investigator, then digitised (p. 206).
Men's maxillomandibular difference: 37.2 mm in Table 2 and the text (p. 207), 37.3 mm in Table 4 (p. 209); Table 2 used. Other values are restated in Tables 3-6 and agree.
